hook: Kenneth Mark Colby was born in 1920 in Waterbury, Connecticut, and trained as a physician, graduating from Yale University in 1941 and Yale Medical School in 1943 before turning to psychoanalysis. In the early 1960s he moved to Stanford University's computer science department, where he began applying computational models to psychiatric theory. There he created PARRY, a natural language program that simulated the conversational patterns of a person with paranoid schizophrenia by weighting incoming statements as threatening or benign and responding with scripted defensive strategies. In 1972 PARRY and Joseph Weizenbaum's ELIZA were connected over the ARPANET at the International Conference on Computer Communications, producing one of the first recorded conversations between two artificial conversational agents. Colby later joined UCLA as a professor of psychiatry with a joint appointment in computer science, continued his research on computational models of mental illness, and died on April 20, 2001, at the age of 81.

quick_facts: Born in 1920 in Waterbury, Connecticut, and died April 20, 2001, at age 81.
Graduated from Yale University in 1941 and Yale Medical School in 1943.
Trained and practiced as a psychoanalyst before moving into computer science.
Joined Stanford University's computer science department in the early 1960s, where he created PARRY.
PARRY exchanged messages with Joseph Weizenbaum's ELIZA over the ARPANET in 1972.
Later became a professor of psychiatry at UCLA with a joint appointment in computer science.

achievements.title: PARRY (1972)
achievements.impact: Modeled the language patterns of paranoid schizophrenia closely enough that psychiatrists reviewing transcripts could distinguish it from a real patient only about as often as chance, an early demonstration of a machine passing a Turing-style test in a clinical setting.

achievements.title: Artificial Paranoia (Colby, Weber and Hilf, 1971)
achievements.impact: Documented PARRY's design and evaluation, giving researchers a rigorous method for testing whether a conversational program's output could be distinguished from a person's.

achievements.title: Computational psychiatry research
achievements.impact: Extended computational modeling into clinical psychiatry, an early example of applying AI methods to the study of mental illness rather than only language or logic.
